{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/sales.csv')

# Verify premises
# 1. 'converted' == 1 means completed checkout — confirmed in documentation
# 2. -1 in customer_age is sentinel — confirmed
# 3. Check for QA orders with revenue = 999999.99
qa_orders = df[df['revenue'] == '999999.99']
print(f'Number of QA orders: {len(qa_orders)}')

# Check if any 'revenue' is non-numeric or malformed
# Convert revenue to float after stripping commas
df['revenue_clean'] = df['revenue'].str.replace(',', '').astype(float)

# Check for any non-numeric values in revenue
non_numeric_revenue = df[~df['revenue'].str.replace(',', '').str.isnumeric()]
print(f'Non-numeric revenue entries: {len(non_numeric_revenue)}')

# Check if any revenue values are suspiciously high (e.g. > 10000)
high_revenue = df[df['revenue_clean'] > 10000]
print(f'Orders with revenue > $10,000: {len(high_revenue)}')

# Inspect the data
print('\nFirst few rows:')
print(df.head())

# Check unique values in key columns
print('\nUnique values in channel:')
print(df['channel'].unique())

print('\nUnique values in customer_segment:')
print(df['customer_segment'].unique())

print('\nUnique values in status:')
print(df['status'].unique())

# Check distribution of 'converted'
print('\nDistribution of converted:')
print(df['converted'].value_counts())

# Check distribution of customer_age
print('\nCustomer age distribution:')
print(df['customer_age'].describe())

# Note: -1 is sentinel for missing age
# We will exclude -1 from mean calculation
# But first, check if there are any other issues with age
print(f'Number of customers with age = -1: {(df["customer_age"] == -1).sum()}')"}
